scenes.heading: Advantages of Batch Processing
scenes.narration: Batch processing offers several practical advantages that keep it central to data engineering despite the rise of streaming.

scenes.heading: Key advantages
bullets: High throughput for very large volumes
Simpler to build and reason about
scenes.narration: Batch processing delivers high throughput because it handles enormous volumes in one pass. It uses compute efficiently by processing data in bulk rather than piece by piece. It is simpler to build and reason about than always-on streaming systems. And it is cost-effective, since jobs can be scheduled during cheaper off-peak hours.

scenes.heading: Batch advantages vs streaming
scenes.narration: Batch excels at huge scale with simpler operations and lower infrastructure cost because it runs only when scheduled. Streaming addresses real-time needs but demands more complex, always-on infrastructure. When your use case tolerates delay, batch's simplicity and efficiency are hard to beat.

scenes.text: Batch processing wins on throughput, simplicity, and cost when instant results aren't required.
scenes.narration: The bottom line is that batch processing wins on throughput, simplicity, and cost whenever your workload can tolerate a scheduled delay.
